gemstat-open-archive.title: UNEP GEMS/Water Global Freshwater Quality Archive: v3 arsenic subset
gemstat-open-archive.publisher: UNEP GEMS/Water Programme, GEMS/Water Data Centre and German Federal Institute of Hydrology
gemstat-open-archive.citation: Heinle, M., Lisniak, D., and Saile, P. (2026). UNEP GEMS/Water Global Freshwater Quality Archive, v3. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18459694
gemstat-open-archive.redistribution: Use for attributed research analysis. The complete third-party archive remains outside Git; this project materializes only a verified arsenic and metadata subset.
scientific_notes: As-Dis, As-Sus and As-Tot are distinct dissolved, suspended and total fractions and must not be merged silently.
The arsenic subset contains both mg/l and µg/l and preserves less-than and greater-than censoring flags.
Most arsenic rows use undefined analysis method code 0; method completeness therefore remains a material comparison limitation.
Three -999.999 and 78 values at or above 1000 mg/l are marked Pending review and must not enter normalized demos or anomaly claims.
Station metadata contain 35 exact duplicate rows across 35 IDs; the adapter preserves both source locators but uses one identical station fact set.
The v3 description claims 22,982 stations and 622 parameters, while the selected metadata files contain 22,981 station rows and 621 parameter rows; the one-record differences remain explicit.
GEMStat is voluntarily contributed and geographically uneven; the arsenic subset covers 33 countries and is not uniform global freshwater coverage.

japan-gsj-geochemical-map.redistribution: Use for attributed research analysis under the GSJ website terms. The complete third-party CSV files remain outside Git.
scientific_notes: This adapter covers the national river-sediment tables only; marine sediment and later surface-soil products remain separate datasets.
The national map is based on fine stream sediment below 180 micrometres and discrete river-network samples, not a regular national grid.
Source coordinates are JGD2000 (EPSG:4612) and must be transformed explicitly before WGS84 map output.
The official web service identifies Hg as ppb and the other registered trace elements as ppm.
Sample ID 78013 occurs twice in both files; the adapter joins by normalized sample ID plus occurrence order and never overwrites a duplicate dictionary key.
The two CSV files do not contain row-level analytical method, detection-limit or quality-flag fields; method evidence must be attached from the cited project publications.

afsis-phase-i-wet-chemistry.title: AfSIS Phase I archived soil samples: wet chemistry data
afsis-phase-i-wet-chemistry.citation: von Fromm, S. F. et al. (2021). Continental-scale controls on soil organic carbon across sub-Saharan Africa. SOIL 7, 305-332. doi:10.5194/soil-7-305-2021. Dataset version 2.0: doi:10.34725/DVN/66BFOB.
afsis-phase-i-wet-chemistry.redistribution: Research-use derived fixtures retain attribution, DOI, source-file hashes and row locators; full publisher files remain outside Git.
scientific_notes: The 2,002 archived samples cover 51 LDSF sentinel sites with 18 country labels and are not a spatially uniform African grid.
Aqua-regia digestion is quasi-total; results must not be mixed with total or other extraction bases without explicit separation.
The source-wide DL and QL apply to the published wet-chemistry batch. Numeric values below them are flagged rather than silently discarded or promoted to detections.
Negative numeric instrument results are retained as evidence-bound source values but excluded from the positive demonstration fixture.
One hundred twenty-six samples lack both latitude and longitude; no coordinate is inferred.
Raw country labels including SAfrica and Zimbambwe are preserved; normalized names are stored separately.
The registered files and related article do not state a coordinate reference system; latitude and longitude are preserved but source_crs remains missing.
The variable workbook labels field As.75 as Arsenic-78 and gives sampling years 2009-2013, while the related article reports 2009-2012; both conflicts remain explicit.
